newsitem.title: USA: Simpson civil trial lawyers prepare closing arguments.
newsitem.headline: Simpson civil trial lawyers prepare closing arguments.

text.p: Attorneys for both sides in the O.J. Simpson civil trial spent Monday preparing closing arguments they will make to the jury starting Tuesday.

Jurors must decide if the former football star is responsible for the deaths of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, who were stabbed to death on the night of June 12, 1994.

Simpson, who was acquitted of murder charges in a criminal trial in October 1995, is being sued in a wrongful-death case brought by the victims' families, who are seeking monetary damages for their loss.

Daniel Petrocelli, who represents Goldman's family and is the plaintiffs' lead attorney, was expected to stress what has been called a "mountain of evidence" against Simpson, as prosecutors did unsuccessfully in the criminal trial.

But this time the plaintiffs have a powerful new weapon that was not available to criminal prosecutors: recently discovered photographs showing Simpson wearing Italian designer Bruno Magli shoes like the ones that left a trail of bloody prints leading from the murder scene outside Nicole Brown Simpson's condominium.

Simpson testified at the trial he had never owned Bruno Maglis. But an FBI expert testified last week that 30 pictures taken of Simpson at a 1993 Buffalo Bills football game were authentic and another FBI expert testified that the shoes Simpson was wearing in the photographs were Bruno Maglis.

Although Simpson's defence contends the photographs were faked, they did not produce their own expert to support that. They did contest one photograph of Simpson taken at the same game by a different photographer, producing an amateur analyst who said he believed it had been altered. But the plaintiffs' expert disagreed, saying that picture was also genuine.
Simpson's defence attorney, Robert Baker, laid out his strategy for closing arguments Friday, saying his theme would be, "If you can't trust the messenger you can't trust the message."
"We are saying the jury should distrust every piece of evidence in this case," Baker told Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki during discussions between lawyers with the jury absent.

Baker has closely followed the criminal defence team's strategy of suggesting that the police investigation was botched and evidence was either planted by police to frame Simpson or was contaminated by sloppy collection procedures.
Petrocelli will be followed in summations by attorney John Kelly, who represents Nicole Brown Simpson's estate, and Michael Brewer, the lawyer for Sharon Rufo, Goldman's mother.
Baker will then deliver his closing statement, after which Petrocelli will have a chance for rebuttal.
Fujisaki promised the jury last week they would be able to start their deliberations on Thursday. The trial started last September with jury selection.
If Simpson loses the case, he faces no threat of jail time but could be forced to pay millions of dollars in damages.
